body: OK, I think data: and about: URLs will always fail during fetching since they are cross-origin per https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#origin (and there is no way to set CORS headers on them). blob: URLs should still work though.
Nope, data: URLs are treated as same origin per https://github.com/whatwg/fetch/commit/6f223de29733e64dbe1dfc6028c6e0a4a5d89398 (https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-main-fetch step 11)

@domenic yes, if `data:` is idempotent/cached it would **NOT** be run twice if someone does something like `alert('foo')` in the Module source and `import(alertFoo);import(alertFoo);`. Such behavior of run once on specifier would be very surprising for data/blob.
@bmeck can you give a more fleshed-out code example of the scenario you are concerned with?

``` js
const specifier = "data:text/javascript;charset=utf-8,document.getElementById%28%27username%27%29.value%3D%27foo%27%3B"

import(specifier); // sets username value to "foo"
import(specifier); // does nothing, has same namespace as previous
```

I see. (With `text/javascript` instead of `text/plain` as otherwise it will fail.)

That will indeed only execute once, with the second one doing nothing. Even if those `import()`s were in different source files. Which is kind of interesting.

I would only expect it to execute once, personally.  Classic scripts execute once per script and module scripts are once per url.

If there were a way to do `eval()` for modules it would fulfill that use-case.

@matthewp I would disagree; I would find the "run once" for any matching source text nature of a data/blob very surprising. It also seems problematic if it only runs once since if it is code generated with the intent to run, it would lead to cache busting by adding random noise and hoping it busts the cache.

I would heavily argue that node would not have data/blob urls work in a permanent based upon matching source text strategy and would hope the browser would do the same if for nothing other than avoiding a mismatch in behavior.

I don't think we have any intention of disallowing blob or data URLs; they are URLs like any other. Remember that they would mostly be used to generate normal, non-side-effecting modules that, like every other module, only run once. For that purpose they are very useful.

@bmeck I don't see why the behavior should be different based on scheme. You agree here that this module should only execute once, right?

``` html
<script type="module" src="https://example.com/foo.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="https://example.com/foo.js"></script>
```

I think data: and/or blob: would be valuable as a way to create modules at runtime, and I would want them to behave like any other module. This would be even more valuable when/if we ever get the ability to do some type of path mapping for bare specifiers.

@domenic you cannot guarantee they are non-side-effecting modules.

@matthewp I consider those separated exactly because they have a different scheme. I don't expect http and https to have the exact same behavior. See things like how cookies work.
Of course, just like with `http:`, we cannot guarantee anything. But we still only execute it once.

I still vehemently will argue that source text vs source location should be
treated differently. Many locations and code generators could produce equal
source text. Data and blob being produced in multiple locations and code
generators are not something I expect to execute only once.

The example from @matthewp used the same scheme. If two identical HTTPS URLs run once, why would two identical data/blob URLs not run once too?

Intent of URI as location vs content. Many things could easily generate
duplicate content and expect evaluation. JSONP is a good example of what
happens when location and content are treated the same. I find it confusing
and flat out illogical that they _should_ act the same. The question here
is should location and content be idempotent in the same way. If code
generators expect to produce blob or data URIs how can they do so in a way
that either ensures execution or does not collide with existing cached
source texts. Due to this odd behavior I heavily vie that data and blob in
my mind are not compatible with ESM idempotency. If I must go so far as to
implement such schemes in node they will not be the same as browsers.

Right, dynamic module creation is a key use of data and blob URLs (just as they are useful for any other dynamic resource creation).

I'll close this since I don't think we'll be changing the spec here to special-case data/blob for modules. They behave the same way here as they do for any other resource on the platform, and have the same use cases. Happy to continue discussion, of course.

I think if they are supported in Web the only thing that must be checked is
that timing is always async, though that would not be true in Node as
things currently look (both a lack of desire to support those schemes and
sync import)
